chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When a man has the capacity for that with which he performs Hajj, then he dismisses it from himself, and he has no excuse that justifies him, then he has left a ruling from the rulings of Islam."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person who has money for Hajj but spends it on other things without a valid excuse?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that the obligation of Hajj becomes binding immediately upon the accumulation of sufficient wealth, provided there is no valid impediment. It emphasizes that diverting these funds for other uses without excuse constitutes a neglect of a fundamental pillar, highlighting the urgency of fulfilling this duty once financial capacity is established.
